$comment: Pins the shipped Go and TypeScript HDF validators to one another on JSON Schema `format`. Both read this file and validate the same documents, so the two halves of this repo cannot disagree about whether a document is valid HDF. Each case names the RFC clause that settles it, because a validator disagreeing with its peer is only half the problem — one of them is also wrong.
$knownDivergence: uri-reference is deliberately absent. gojsonschema accepts a space, '<', '|', '^' and backtick inside one where ajv rejects them, so the shipped pair still disagrees there. It is left recorded rather than closed because neither library is RFC 3986-exact — ajv accepts a double quote the RFC excludes — so matching either would import its idiosyncrasies rather than make one correct. That behaviour is already pinned for both libraries in hdf-converters/shared/testdata/format-assertion-cases.json, which uses the same two libraries; re-asserting it here would duplicate a pin, not add one.

cases.name: uppercase uuid
cases.why: RFC 4122 §3: generators emit lowercase, but all input is accepted case-insensitively

cases.name: uuid with a padded value
cases.why: surrounding whitespace is not part of the UUID grammar

cases.name: not a uuid at all
cases.why: a name is not a UUID

cases.name: lowercase t and z in a date-time
cases.why: RFC 3339 §5.6 NOTE: lowercase t and z are permitted

cases.name: leap second in a date-time
cases.why: RFC 3339 §5.7: second 60 is a leap second and is legal

cases.name: bare date where a date-time belongs
cases.why: RFC 3339 date-time requires full-date T full-time; a bare date is not one

cases.name: date-time with an offset
cases.why: a numeric offset is as valid as Z

cases.name: date-time with no offset at all
space where the T separator belongs
cases.why: RFC 3339 §5.6 permits a space only by mutual agreement; HDF's canonical timestamp requires the T, so every validator in this repo requires it — ajv is tightened to match Go rather than the reverse

cases.name: urn:uuid: prefixed identifier
cases.why: ajv accepts the urn:uuid: form, so the Go peer must too
